Plot Lorentz Coordinates on the Hyperboloid

Source: R/plot.R
plot_lhwr_hyperboloid.Rd

Visualize Lorentz hyperboloid coordinates on the upper sheet z0 = sqrt(1 + z1^2 + z2^2). This plot emphasizes the geometry used by LHWR estimation: observations live on the Lorentz hyperboloid, and local neighborhoods are defined by Lorentz-hyperbolic distances. For readable two-dimensional displays, use plot_lhwr_poincare_map().

Usage

plot_lhwr_hyperboloid(
  Z,
  values = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  sizes = NULL,
  title = "LHWR Lorentz hyperboloid view",
  value_label = NULL,
  point_palette = "Blue-Red 3",
  surface_col = "#D7E8F0",
  surface_alpha = 0.55,
  surface_border = "#FFFFFF",
  theta = 38,
  phi = 24,
  expand = 0.8,
  grid_n = 55L,
  surface_quantile = "auto",
  point_size = 1.1,
  show_labels = FALSE,
  n_label = 30L,
  mar = c(1.4, 1.4, 2.8, 0.8),
  label_cex = NULL,
  colorbar_cex = NULL,
  title_cex = NULL,
  point_min = NULL,
  point_max = NULL,
  plot_control = NULL,
  show_colorbar = TRUE,
  output_file = NULL,
  device = c("auto", "png", "eps", "pdf"),
  width = 7,
  height = 6,
  res = 220,
  ...
)

Arguments

Z

An n x 3 Lorentz hyperboloid coordinate matrix with columns (z0, z1, z2).

values

Optional numeric vector used to color points. If omitted, the hyperbolic radius acosh(z0) is used.

labels

Optional point labels.

sizes

Optional numeric vector used to scale point sizes.

title

Plot title. Use NULL for manuscript-style panels.

value_label

Label for the colorbar. If omitted, a sensible default is chosen from values.

point_palette

HCL palette for numeric values.

surface_col

Color of the hyperboloid surface.

surface_alpha

Transparency of the hyperboloid surface.

surface_border

Grid-line color for the surface.

theta, phi

Perspective angles passed to graphics::persp().

expand

Expansion factor passed to graphics::persp().

grid_n

Number of grid points per axis used to draw the surface.

surface_quantile

Quantile in (0, 1] used to set the displayed surface extent from abs(z1) and abs(z2), or "auto". The automatic setting keeps the full range unless a few extreme coordinates would make the hyperboloid surface visually too large. Point coordinates are not changed.

point_size

Fixed point size used when sizes is omitted.

show_labels

Logical; draw labels for selected points.

n_label

Number of labels to draw when show_labels = TRUE.

mar

Base graphics margins passed to graphics::par() for the hyperboloid panel.

label_cex, colorbar_cex, title_cex

Character sizes. These can also be supplied through plot_control. For label_cex, "auto" chooses a small value from the number of observations when labels are drawn.

point_min, point_max

Minimum and maximum point sizes when sizes is supplied.

plot_control

Optional list created by lhwr_plot_control(). Direct arguments such as label_cex or colorbar_cex override values in this list.

show_colorbar

Logical; draw a numeric colorbar.

output_file

Optional path. If supplied, the plot is written to this file. The device is inferred from the file extension unless device is supplied.

device

Output device: "auto", "png", "eps", or "pdf".

width, height

Output size in inches when output_file is supplied.

res

Raster resolution for PNG output and fallback resolution for EPS.

...

Additional arguments passed to graphics::persp().

Value

Invisibly returns a data frame containing the plotted Lorentz coordinates, hyperbolic radii, values, and point sizes.

Examples

H <- simulate_H2(30, r_max = 2)
plot_lhwr_hyperboloid(H$Z, values = H$r, title = NULL)
